Almost all accepted students in this dataset planned to study full-time, so attending part-time pushed the prediction further toward failure. Your first-year standing also mattered, though less: you were in the third decile versus an accepted average near the sixth, another signal that your early law-school grades were weaker than those of successful applicants. Together these factors outweighed other information and produced the rejection. To improve your chances, focus first on raising your academic performance and class standing, especially in later years. Consider whether full-time study is feasible.
